questions.passage: At dawn, Mama Nkechi and her daughter, Ada, set up a stall near Ariaria Market in Aba. The previous night's rain had soaked one carton of detergent, so they spread the sachets on a mat to dry. Although business was slow, Mama Nkechi remained undaunted. She had saved ₦48,000 since January, and she planned to use part of it to buy a second-hand freezer for selling chilled water. Ada, who had just finished secondary school, kept records of every sale in a small exercise book. When a customer complained that a sachet was torn, Ada replaced it at once and apologised politely. By noon, the two traders had sold more than half of their stock. Mama Nkechi told her daughter that patience and honesty had built the small business, and she urged Ada never to despise humble beginnings. The young woman promised to remain diligent, even if profits were small at first.
questions.q: As used in the passage, the word 'undaunted' most nearly means ______.
questions.explanation: In the passage, business is slow, yet Mama Nkechi 'remained undaunted', so the word describes her refusal to be discouraged. 'Physically exhausted' refers to tiredness rather than courage, and 'unnecessarily proud' suggests arrogance, which the context does not support.

questions.q: In the passage, the use of 'had saved' in 'She had saved ₦48,000 since January' shows that the saving ______.
options: would be completed at a future time
was still going on when the narrator was speaking
was completed before another past action in the story
started and continued up to the present moment
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had saved' presents an action completed before a later point in the past, here before she planned to buy the freezer. 'Started and continued up to the present moment' would require the present perfect form 'has saved'.

questions.q: As used in the passage, the word 'despise' is most nearly opposite in meaning to ______.
questions.explanation: 'Despise' means to regard with contempt, so its opposite is 'respect'. 'Ignore' is closer to neglect and does not express the opposite of contempt.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'equitable' as used in the sentence: The market women praised the council for introducing an equitable system of allocating stalls.
questions.explanation: 'Equitable' describes something just and impartial, so 'fair' is the nearest meaning. 'Profitable' relates to gain and 'temporary' relates to duration, neither of which captures justice in allocation.

questions.q: Choose the correct option to complete the sentence: The newly elected chairman, as well as his two advisers, ______ expected to address the traders tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun 'chairman'; the phrase 'as well as his two advisers' is parenthetical and does not make it plural. Hence the singular verb 'is' is required, while 'are' would wrongly agree with 'advisers'.

questions.q: Which word ends with the same final consonant sound as the 'gh' in 'laugh'?
questions.explanation: The 'gh' in 'laugh' is pronounced /f/, and 'enough' also ends with the /f/ sound. 'Bough', 'through' and 'dough' end with vowel sounds, so they do not share that final consonant.

questions.q: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as the 'ch' in 'chorus'?
questions.explanation: The 'ch' in 'chorus' is pronounced /k/, and 'chemist' also begins with /k/. 'Chair', 'chief' and 'cheque' begin with the /tʃ/ sound.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'i' in 'sit'?
questions.explanation: The 'i' in 'sit' represents the short vowel /ɪ/, which appears in the first syllable of 'busy'. 'Site' and 'side' have /aɪ/, while 'seat' has /iː/.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'oi' in 'coin'?
questions.explanation: The 'oi' in 'coin' is the diphthong /ɔɪ/, which is also heard in 'toy'. 'Tie' has /aɪ/, 'toe' has /oʊ/, and 'town' has /aʊ/.

questions.q: Choose the correct spelling to complete the sentence: The council has begun the construction of a new ______ for physically challenged pupils.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'dormitory', with the letters d-o-r-m-i-t-o-r-y. The other forms either change the vowel after 't' or omit the 'r' after 'o', so they are misspellings.

questions.q: If the principal says that the new library project is still up in the air, he means that it is ______.
questions.explanation: The idiom 'up in the air' means unsettled or not yet decided. It does not refer to the building being open or completed. 'Certain to fail' is a different meaning from uncertainty about a decision.

questions.q: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the second syllable?
questions.explanation: The word 'important' has its strongest beat on the second syllable. The words 'regular', 'wonderful' and 'minister' are normally stressed on their first syllables.

questions.q: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Had the driver obeyed the traffic warden, the accident ______ avoided.
questions.explanation: The sentence is a third conditional with 'Had' at the beginning, so the main clause needs 'would have been' before the past participle 'avoided'. 'Would be' and 'will have been' do not match the past unreal condition. 'Had been avoided' would make two past perfect clauses without the required modal meaning.

questions.q: During the meeting, Amina was all ears when the chairman spoke about the scholarship. What does 'all ears' mean?
questions.explanation: 'All ears' describes someone who is paying full attention and eager to hear. It does not mean talking, sleeping or refusing to listen. The context of the chairman speaking about a scholarship supports attentive listening.

questions.q: Which of the following words is stressed on the first syllable?
questions.explanation: The word 'market' has its primary stress on the first syllable. The words 'begin', 'forget' and 'enjoy' normally carry primary stress on the second syllable.

questions.q: After the team lost its first two matches, the coach's message gave the players a shot in the arm. This means that the message ______.
questions.explanation: A 'shot in the arm' is an idiom for something that gives renewed energy or encouragement. In this context, the coach's message lifted the players rather than confused or threatened them. Being forgotten or warning of punishment does not fit the meaning of the expression.

questions.q: In the sentence 'halima bought the fabric in jos yesterday', which word should be stressed to contradict the suggestion that she bought the fabric in abuja?
questions.explanation: Stress falls on 'jos' because it is the place that contrasts with the suggested 'abuja'. Stressing 'halima', 'fabric' or 'yesterday' would correct a different mistaken idea, not the place of purchase.

questions.passage: When Amina opened her tailoring shop in Jos, she kept no written records. She trusted her memory and wrote only the names of customers on scraps of paper. At first, the shop was busy, but after six months she could not tell which fabrics sold fastest or how much she spent on thread. Sometimes she borrowed from the shop's daily takings to pay her younger brother's school fees, promising to replace the money later. When a customer demanded a refund for a dress that had been delayed, Amina discovered that she had only four hundred naira in the box though she had sold cloth worth far more that week. Her friend, Malam Bello, advised her to separate business money from household money and to record every sale, however small. Amina started a simple exercise book, listing each customer, the amount paid and the balance owed. By December, she could see that Ankara materials brought more profit than plain cotton, and she used the naira she would have wasted on slow-selling stock to buy more Ankara. Her shop expanded, and she employed a second apprentice.
questions.q: According to the passage, what did Amina discover when a customer demanded a refund for a delayed dress?
options: The Ankara materials had spoilt in the shop.
She had only four hundred naira in the box although she had sold cloth worth far more that week.
She had forgotten the customer's name.
Her friend Malam Bello had taken the day's takings.
questions.explanation: The passage states that when the refund was demanded, Amina found only four hundred naira in the box despite having sold cloth worth far more that week. This shows the danger of not keeping proper records of sales and spending.

questions.passage: When Amina opened her tailoring shop in Jos, she kept no written records. She trusted her memory and wrote only the names of customers on scraps of paper. questions.q: Which detail from the passage best shows that Amina's shop expanded?
options: She listed each customer in a simple exercise book.
She paid her younger brother's school fees from the shop's takings.
She kept no written records at first.
questions.explanation: Taking on a second apprentice is the clearest evidence in the passage that the business had grown. Keeping no records, using shop money for school fees and starting an exercise book do not by themselves show expansion.

questions.q: When the bursar said that the principal had his hands tied over the new fee, he meant that the principal
options: supported the new fee without any condition.
had injured his hands while signing forms.
was too busy to discuss the new fee.
was not free to act because of rules or other authorities.
questions.explanation: The expression 'had his hands tied' means being prevented from acting freely, usually by rules or higher authorities. It does not refer to physical injury, busyness or unconditional support.

questions.q: After the meeting, the youth leader said that the chairperson had thrown cold water on their plan. The youth leader meant that the chairperson had
options: asked for the plan to be kept in a cool place.
poured water on the written plan by accident.
questions.explanation: To 'throw cold water on' a plan is to discourage it or make it seem less likely to succeed. The expression is figurative and has nothing to do with actual water or keeping documents cool.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: Each of the market women ___ required to present her trading permit before the end of the month.
questions.explanation: The subject 'each' is singular even though it is followed by 'of the market women', so it takes the singular verb 'is'. The phrase 'of the market women' does not change the singular agreement of 'each'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: Neither the secretary nor the chairperson ___ willing to sign the minutes.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is 'the chairperson', a singular noun. Therefore the singular verb 'is' is required; 'have' would also fail because the sentence needs a form of 'be' before 'willing'.

questions.passage: When Mama Nkechi's shop in Awka was burgled last March, she did not wait for the police alone. She joined six other traders to form a weekly savings group called Otu Uche. Each member paid ₦2,000 every Friday, and the group agreed that any member hit by theft or fire could borrow up to ₦40,000 without interest. The money was kept in a metal box with three padlocks because the nearest bank was a long bus ride away. By August, the group had helped two members replace stolen goods and had paid part of the hospital bill of a trader's child. Mama Nkechi now keeps a small record book and reads out the balance every Friday. The traders say the group has taught them to save before trouble comes, rather than to borrow at high interest after a loss. Their next plan is to rent a lockable stall at the main market.
questions.q: According to the passage, the traders formed Otu Uche mainly to ______
options: borrow money from the nearest bank at low interest
buy a lockable stall for every member
support one another after losses such as theft or fire
pay the hospital bills of all traders' children
questions.explanation: The passage says the group was formed after a burglary and allowed members hit by theft or fire to borrow without interest; its purpose was therefore mutual support after losses. Paying every trader's child's hospital bill and buying a stall for every member go beyond what the passage states.

questions.q: The group kept its money in a metal box because ______
options: the nearest bank was a long bus ride away
members did not trust one another with the records
the police refused to guard the market
the box was cheaper than opening a bank account
questions.explanation: The passage states directly that the metal box was used because the nearest bank was a long bus ride away. The police, the cost of opening an account and lack of trust in records are not given as reasons.

questions.q: By August, the group had used part of its money to ______
options: rent a lockable stall at the main market
help pay a trader's child's hospital bill
buy a grinding machine for Mama Nkechi
build a new police post near the market
questions.explanation: The passage records that by August the group had helped replace stolen goods and paid part of a trader's child's hospital bill. Renting a lockable stall is only a future plan, and the police post and grinding machine are not mentioned.

questions.q: Which word begins with the same consonant sound as the 'g' in 'germ'?
questions.explanation: 'Germ' begins with the /dʒ/ sound, and 'journey' also begins with /dʒ/. 'Game', 'guest' and 'goal' begin with the hard /g/ sound.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'ea' in 'bread'?
questions.explanation: The 'ea' in 'bread' is pronounced /e/, and 'head' has the same vowel sound. 'Bead' has /iː/, while 'break' and 'great' have /eɪ/.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'u' in 'full'?
questions.explanation: The 'u' in 'full' is the short /ʊ/ sound, as in 'book'. 'Food' and 'flute' have /uː/, while 'cut' has /ʌ/.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelled word to complete the sentence: The accountant was asked to ______ the figures before the audit.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'verify', which means to check or confirm accuracy. The forms 'varify', 'verrify' and 'verfy' are misspellings.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The committee praised the engineer for her ______ in handling the difficult project. (efficient)
questions.explanation: After the possessive 'her', a noun is needed, and 'efficiency' is the correct noun form. 'Efficiently' is an adverb, 'efficient' is an adjective, and 'efficience' is not the standard spelling.

questions.q: The chairperson insisted that every member ______ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: After 'insisted that' in a demand or requirement, standard English uses the base form 'be'. The present, past and plural forms 'is', 'was' and 'are' do not fit this subjunctive construction.

questions.passage: When Ngozi opened her small bakery in Awka, she sold only plain loaves at ₦900 each. Customers came, but many complained that a loaf went stale before the family could finish it. Ngozi's aunt, a retired caterer, advised her to bake smaller loaves twice a day instead of large ones once. Ngozi resisted at first, fearing the extra cost of gas, but she tried the plan for two weeks. The complaints stopped. Encouraged, she added meat pies and doughnuts, and began writing every sale in an exercise book. By December she had hired two assistants and bought a second oven. She now says the exercise book taught her more than any advice, because it showed her that doughnuts sold fastest on Saturday mornings, so she began baking extra on Fridays. Her aunt still visits, not to advise, but to buy.
questions.q: According to the passage, what was the first complaint Ngozi's customers made?
options: The meat pies were more expensive than the bread.
The price of a loaf was too high for most families.
A loaf went stale before it could be finished.
The bread was often sold out before noon.
questions.explanation: The passage states that customers came but many complained that a loaf went stale before the family could finish it. Nothing in the passage reports complaints about price or about bread selling out. The meat pies are mentioned only after the complaints had stopped, so they cannot be the first complaint.

questions.passage: When Ngozi opened her small bakery in Awka, she sold only plain loaves at ₦900 each. Customers came, but many complained that a loaf went stale before the family could finish it. Her aunt still visits, not to advise, but to buy.
questions.q: Why did Ngozi hesitate to follow her aunt's advice?
options: She feared the extra cost of gas.
She had no money to buy an exercise book.
She believed customers preferred large loaves.
She did not trust her aunt's experience as a caterer.
questions.explanation: The passage says Ngozi resisted at first because she feared the extra cost of gas that baking twice a day would require. Her trust in her aunt is not questioned, and the exercise book is mentioned later, after the advice had already been tried. Nothing in the passage suggests she thought customers preferred large loaves.

questions.q: Which detail from the passage best shows that Ngozi's bakery had expanded?
options: She hired two assistants and bought a second oven.
Her aunt still visits the bakery to buy bread.
She stopped baking large loaves of bread.
She began writing every sale in an exercise book.
questions.explanation: Hiring two assistants and buying a second oven is clear evidence of growth in staff and equipment. Writing sales in an exercise book is a record-keeping change that could be done by any trader, large or small. A relative buying bread shows only that the bakery has a customer, not that the business has expanded.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Chidi decided to bite the bullet and apologise to his landlord', what does the expression mean?
options: He accepted an unpleasant situation and did what had to be done.
He postponed the matter until a more convenient day.
He offered the landlord money to forget the matter.
He spoke angrily and refused to listen to anybody.
questions.explanation: To bite the bullet is to face something unpleasant bravely instead of avoiding it, which fits Chidi's decision to apologise even though he found it painful. Postponing the matter is the opposite of acting, and the expression says nothing about anger or about offering money.

questions.q: When the figures in the ledger did not add up, the auditor began to smell a rat. This means that the auditor ______.
options: became suspicious that something was wrong
decided to ignore the errors in the ledger
asked for a completely new ledger
noticed a bad odour in the office
questions.explanation: To smell a rat is to suspect that something is wrong or dishonest, and the figures that would not add up gave the auditor good reason for suspicion. The expression is figurative, so it has nothing to do with an actual bad smell. Ignoring the errors would be the opposite of what a suspicious auditor does.

questions.q: The contractor was accused of cutting corners on the road project. What does this mean?
options: He used the most expensive materials available.
He did the work cheaply and carelessly in order to save money.
He employed more labourers than the project required.
He completed the work far ahead of the deadline.
questions.explanation: To cut corners is to do something in the easiest, cheapest or quickest way, usually by skimping on quality, so the contractor was accused of careless, money-saving work. Finishing early or employing extra labourers is not what the idiom describes. Using the most expensive materials would be the opposite of cutting corners.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Adaeze borrowed the book from the library yesterday', which word would be stressed to contradict the suggestion that she bought the book?
questions.explanation: Emphatic stress falls on the word that carries the point being contrasted, and here the contrast is between buying and borrowing, so 'borrowed' must be stressed. Stressing 'book' would contrast the book with some other item, and stressing 'library' or 'yesterday' would shift the contrast to place or time rather than to how she obtained the book.

questions.q: No sooner had the bell rung than the students left the hall. What does this mean?
options: The students waited a while before leaving the hall.
The students left the hall before the bell rang.
The students left the hall immediately the bell rang.
The bell rang after all the students had left the hall.
questions.explanation: The construction 'no sooner ... than' shows that the second action followed the first at once, so the students left the moment the bell rang. It cannot mean they left before the bell rang or waited for a while, since that would reverse or weaken the sequence expressed. The sentence clearly places the ringing of the bell before the departure.

questions.passage: When Mrs Adaeze opened her small shop in Abakaliki, many neighbours doubted that it would survive. The road in front of the shop was dusty, and customers often complained about the heat. Instead of giving up, she used her savings to buy a large umbrella and two benches. She also began to keep a notebook in which she recorded every customer's complaint and suggestion. Her manner was cordial, and she listened patiently even when a buyer grumbled about the price of garri. Within a year, her little shop had become a favourite meeting point for traders in the area. One Saturday, a heavy rain flooded the road, but Mrs Adaeze calmly moved her goods to higher shelves and lent umbrellas to customers who lived nearby. Her foresight saved her stock. Today, young people in Abakaliki often ask her how she built her business, and she tells them that patience and careful planning are more valuable than loud advertisement.
questions.q: As used in the passage, the word 'cordial' most nearly means
questions.explanation: In the passage, 'cordial' describes Mrs Adaeze's warm and friendly manner towards customers. 'Anxious', 'formal' and 'displeased' do not convey this welcoming attitude.

questions.q: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'patiently' as used in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage says she listened 'patiently', meaning calmly and without irritation. 'Impatiently' is the direct opposite, while 'quietly', 'carefully' and 'slowly' describe manner but not the opposite of patience.

Today, young people in Abakaliki often ask her how she built her business, and she tells them that patience and careful planning are more valuable than loud advertisement.
questions.q: As used in the passage, 'foresight' most nearly means
questions.explanation: Her 'foresight' is the careful planning that made her move goods before the flood and lend umbrellas. It means 'forethought', not generosity, wealth or stubbornness.

questions.q: Each of the farmers who attended the workshop in Jos ___ a certificate of participation.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'Each', which is singular, so it takes a singular verb. The past context of the workshop makes 'received' the suitable singular past form, while 'have received', 'are receiving' and 'were receiving' do not agree with the singular subject or the time.

questions.q: If the trader had known that the price of rice would fall, he ___ the goods.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional sentence: the if-clause uses 'had known', so the result clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle. 'Would not have bought' completes it correctly, while the other forms do not match the hypothetical past situation.

questions.q: Which word ends with the same final consonant sound as the last sound in 'cloth'?
questions.explanation: 'Cloth' ends with the voiceless /θ/ sound, and 'breath' ends with the same sound. 'Breathe', 'though' and 'smooth' end with the voiced /ð/ sound.

questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as the 'u' in 'put'?
questions.explanation: The 'u' in 'put' represents the short /ʊ/ sound, and 'could' contains the same vowel sound. 'Boot' and 'mood' have /uː/, while 'flood' has /ʌ/.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The local government has approved the ______ of the old market road.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is rehabilitation, which means the restoration of something to good condition. The other forms double or omit letters in the word.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of the word in brackets to complete the sentence: The chairman praised the young trader for the ______ (persist) she showed despite the initial losses.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a noun after the article and before the clause she showed, so persistence is the correct form. Persistent is an adjective, persistently is an adverb, and persisting is a participle or gerund.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word to complete the sentence: The auditor could not explain the sudden ______ of funds from the local government treasury.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is disappearance. The wrong forms contain an extra s, a missing p, or a misplaced e in the ending.

questions.q: It is high time the government ______ greater attention to rural roads.
questions.explanation: After the expression it is high time, standard usage takes a past simple verb for a present or urgent matter. The correct sentence is It is high time the government paid greater attention to rural roads.

questions.q: Not until the chairman arrived ______ the meeting begin.
questions.explanation: A negative expression such as not until at the beginning of a sentence causes inversion. Since the meeting began in the past, the auxiliary did is needed before the subject and the base verb begin.

questions.q: The success of the campaign will depend largely ______ the support of market leaders.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition after depend is on. The expression is depend on someone or something, not depend in, depend for, or depend with in this context.

questions.q: When Mama Nkechi heard the rumour about a new tax, she told her customers to take it with a pinch of salt. What did she mean?
options: They should report the rumour to the tax office.
They should add salt to the rumour.
They should believe the rumour at once.
They should not accept the rumour completely.
questions.explanation: To take something with a pinch of salt means to treat it with doubt rather than accepting it completely. Mama Nkechi was warning her customers not to believe the rumour fully.

questions.q: At the meeting in Ibadan, the proposed market levy became a bone of contention among the traders. This means that the levy ______.
questions.explanation: A bone of contention is a subject over which people disagree strongly. The proposed levy therefore caused serious argument among the traders.

questions.q: Choose the word that is stressed differently from the other three.
questions.explanation: Borrow has its primary stress on the first syllable, while begin, forget, and allow have their primary stress on the second syllable. Therefore borrow is the word with a different stress pattern.

questions.q: Chidi: Did Ada buy the bag for her sister? Ngozi: No, she bought it for her mother. Which word in Ngozi's reply should receive emphatic stress to correct the mistaken information about the person the bag was bought for?
questions.explanation: The contrast is between sister and mother. Stressing mother corrects the mistaken information by making it clear that the bag was bought for the mother, not the sister.

questions.passage: When Ifeoma started selling poultry feed in Aba, she kept her stock in the front room of her small apartment. Customers came mostly by word of mouth, and she recorded sales in a notebook. The arrangement worked until the rainy season, when dampness spoiled several bags of feed. Worse, a customer who had bought two bags on credit claimed he had paid, and Ifeoma, trusting memory, had not written the transaction down. The dispute did not reach the police, but it cost her the customer and a good deal of pride. Her neighbour, Mama Nkechi, advised her to separate the feed from the living area and to issue receipts for every sale, however small. Ifeoma rented a dry store behind the market, bought a cheap receipt book and began to mark each bag with the date it arrived. By December, she had not only recovered her losses but had also won back the doubtful customer, who returned after seeing how carefully her records were kept. She later said that the best lesson came not from the profit she made but from the quarrel she avoided.
questions.q: According to the passage, what led to the dispute between Ifeoma and a customer?
options: Several bags of feed were spoiled by dampness in the rainy season.
Ifeoma refused to issue a receipt after the customer paid in full.
The customer claimed he had paid for two bags of feed that Ifeoma had not recorded as credit.
Mama Nkechi advised her to separate the feed from the living area.
questions.explanation: The passage says the customer claimed he had paid, while Ifeoma had not written the credit transaction down. The dampness caused loss, but it was not the cause of the dispute with the customer.

questions.q: According to the passage, what two things did Mama Nkechi advise Ifeoma to do?
options: Stop selling feed on credit and employ a sales assistant.
Move the business to a dry store behind the market and buy a receipt book.
Record only large sales and count the stock every December.
Keep the feed away from the living area and issue receipts for every sale.
questions.explanation: Mama Nkechi advised Ifeoma to separate the feed from the living area and to issue receipts for every sale, however small. Renting the dry store and buying a receipt book were Ifeoma's own later actions.

questions.q: According to the passage, what did Ifeoma do with each bag after she rented the dry store?

She sold it to the doubtful customer on credit.
She wrote the buyer's name on every receipt only.
She moved it back to her front room at night.
